title: Critical Power: An Important Fatigue Threshold in Exercise Physiology
authors: Poole DC, Burnley M, Vanhatalo A, Rossiter HB, Jones AM
population: Review of the critical power (CP) and W' concept across species, exercise modalities and muscle groups (power-based analogue of critical speed and D')
findings: The hyperbolic power-duration relationship is rigorous and highly conserved across species, forms of exercise and muscle groups; for modalities such as cycling it resolves to two parameters, CP (asymptote) and W' (work doable above CP).
CP separates intensity domains within which physiological responses can (below CP) or cannot (above CP) be stabilised.
Above CP, tolerable duration is predicted by W' until W' is expended, VO2max is attained and intolerance is manifested.
Setting intensity relative to CP unifies the profile of systemic and intramuscular responses better than calibrating to metabolically distant parameters such as lactate threshold or VO2max.
limitations: Narrative review framed mainly on cycling; applicability to running is by analogy (critical speed and D'); no runner data or numbers in the abstract.
implications: Model hard sessions with critical speed (CS) and D' (running analogues of CP and W'): intensity above CS draws down D' and is time-limited; intensity below CS can be physiologically stable.
Use CS as the heavy-severe boundary in the zone model and budget interval volume above CS against D' within a session.

verification.notes: Crossref title 'Critical Power', vol 48 pp 2320-2334; Europe PMC carries full title. Abstract confirms findings.
